analyticalMisses.summary: PRIMARY MISS. Actual $19.65 at 50c (+100). LOSS. The manual analysis independently estimated approximately 62-66% fair and explicitly identified this as the position where substantial size was justified -- that confidence was too aggressive. The analysis overweighted 19 strikeouts in Javier's prior 18 innings, a recent six-inning workload, and apparent post-return improvement, while insufficiently penalizing post-shoulder uncertainty, small post-return sample size, workload/batters-faced volatility, exact pitch-count/leash uncertainty, opponent contact quality, and regression risk in recent K rate. The >12-percentage-point divergence between the independent estimate and the market (62-66% vs. a 50c/+100 market-implied probability) should have triggered stronger skepticism rather than increased conviction. Process grade: D+. This bet is NOT classified as an acceptable variance loss -- the confidence estimate itself is the finding, independent of the coin having landed on LOSS.

Actual $11.77 at 45c (+122). LOSS. Combined with the Ian Seymour 6+ Ks position (same game), this created same-game exposure to both starting pitchers producing sufficient strikeout/workload outcomes -- correlated, not independent, session risk. If tightening the card, Hancock should have been the first cut before Seymour.

analyticalMisses.bet: CIN full-game ML YES + Brady Singer 5+ Ks YES (Cincinnati cluster)
analyticalMisses.summary: CIN full-game ML ($15.72, LOSS) and Brady Singer 5+ Ks ($11.78, LOSS) both lost. Flagged for audit: whether both relied too heavily on the same Cincinnati-favorable game-script thesis, and whether the independent edge on each leg separately justified the combined $27.50 exposure, rather than treating them as one correlated bucket.

Only $1.94 risked, so sizing was appropriately tiny. LOSS. However, cheap longshot price alone (11c) is not itself evidence of value -- this position needs an explicit scoring-distribution / tie-probability edge to be justified as +EV rather than merely inexpensive, consistent with the recurring three-way F5/F7-tie risk pattern already noted in prior EdgeLab postmortems.

processErrors.summary: Six pitcher-strikeout contracts (Brady Singer, Jacob Misiorowski x2, Ian Seymour, Emerson Hancock, Cristian Javier) consumed $75.64 -- approximately 34.6% of total session risk -- and returned a -33.47% ROI (2-4, net -$25.32). This is a single-session finding, not proof pitcher-K props are inherently -EV; it is preserved here as a scoped investigation into workload modeling, batters-faced distributions, pitch-count uncertainty, manager-hook modeling, opponent contact/strikeout-rate distributions, rung selection, and correlated/repeated game-script exposure across same-day pitcher-K positions.

TB@SEA carried strikeout exposure on both starting pitchers (Seymour WIN, Hancock LOSS) -- same-game, same-market-family exposure to two different pitchers' workload outcomes. If reducing the card, Hancock (the LOSS) should have been the first position cut, not a coin-flip choice between the two.

CIN full-game ML and Brady Singer 5+ Ks (both LOSS, both CIN@WSH) may have shared a single underlying Cincinnati-favorable game-script thesis rather than two independently-edged positions -- flagged for audit rather than resolved here; the archived pipeline data available to this postmortem does not itself carry a documented correlation-group tag for these two bets.

CIN@WSH NRFI (NO at 47c) WON, returning +$10.70. The Aug 9 pipeline is known to paper-cap RFI recommendations elsewhere when first-inning-specific xERA is missing (existing repository behavior, lib.edgelab -- not verified against this specific game in this session). Recorded as an open confidence/process question despite the win, not resolved either way.

Every one of the 19 tickers in this batch settled cleanly (settlementStatus=SETTLED, zero SETTLEMENT_UNRESOLVED) and the settled WIN/LOSS record independently reproduces the user's screenshot-reported 12-7 record exactly, with no discrepancies. Each bet's objective status/result on the canonical ledger comes exclusively from this real settlement pipeline -- never fabricated, never inferred from the user's screenshots. Separately, each bet's exact dollar returnAmount/netProfitLoss (which the ledger's own derived formula does not reproduce exactly, due to Kalshi's whole-contract rounding -- e.g. the NRFI leg's formula-derived net P&L is $11.06 vs. the user's confirmed $10.70) was recorded via lib.edgelab.bets.confirm_realized_return (confirmedReceiptSource=MANUAL_POSTMORTEM_RECEIPT), which never touches the objective result/status fields -- exactly the intended separation between objective settlement outcome and confirmed real cash receipt.
